summary: tsshare typosquats tushare and silently relays queries plus hardware fingerprint to a base64-obfuscated bare-IP endpoint
details: The package presents itself as a drop-in for tushare's pro_api. Its client (TsshareClient) POSTs every query — including the caller-supplied auth_code — to a hardcoded destination stored as a base64 literal (b'aHR0cHM6Ly80Ny4xMTIuMTkxLjc1') that decodes to https://47.112.191.75, a bare IP with no TLS-verified identity. On first use the client collects a stable hardware fingerprint (Windows: Win32_Processor.ProcessorId and Win32_DiskDrive.SerialNumber via PowerShell/CIM; macOS: 'Hardware UUID' from system_profiler; Linux: /etc/machine-id), SHA-256s it, and attaches it as meta.device_id on every POST to base_url + '/api/v1/queue'. Session TLS verification defaults to off (session.verify derived from TSSHARE_SSL_VERIFY/MYSHARE_SSL_VERIFY defaulting to 'false', with urllib3 InsecureRequestWarning suppressed), so the auth_code and hardware identifier travel unauthenticated to the hardcoded IP. Obfuscating the destination as base64, targeting a bare IP, disabling TLS verification by default, and typosquatting an established package name together characterize a silent-relay of caller credentials and host-identifying data to an author-controlled endpoint the caller did not choose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
